newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portuguese shares sink with other markets.
newsitem.headline: Portuguese shares sink with other markets.

text.p: 1735 GMT - Portuguese shares sank with other markets following remarks by Fed Chairman Alan Greenspan signalling that the central bank was moving towards tightening credit, possibly as soon as next week. Dealers noted turnover of more than 2.8 million shares in Banco Portugues de Investimento. Turnover in the cash market was 12.9 billion escudos, slightly above the recent daily average. Dealers said they were uncertain about the trend tomorrow and that a slight recovery was possible after the 3.5 percent fall of the PSI20 .PSI20 index of 20 leading stocks over the past four days. "It is difficult to predict trends at such an uncertain time," said one operator. "There could be a recovery tomorrow, but not by much. Everything depends on the close of New York today."

* Portuguese paper firm Inapa-Investimentos, Participacoes e Gestao expects to post a consolidated net profit of about two billion escudos in 1997 and sales of around 60 billion escudos, its president Vasco Pessanha said.
"We think the results (consolidated net profit) in 1997 should double those of 1996," Vasco Pessanha told reporters.
Inapa's 1996 profits rose 200 percent year-on-year to 1.053 billion escudos, while sales fell 18 percent to 40.5 billion escudos.
